Name: Autonomous Underwater Navigation Systems
Problem statement: Modern UUVs typically rely on periodic position updates by surfacing to connect with GNSS or Starlink, which can compromise stealth and reduce efficiency. The challenge here is to develop innovative approaches for truly autonomous underwater navigation that allows precise delivery of payloads to destination points without surfacing. Communication methods are secondary; the primary goal is reliable, accurate underwater navigation.

Name: Challenges in Electronic Warfare: Detecting Radar Systems
Problem statement:
Radar systems send out electromagnetic waves and listen to the reflected waves to scan their environment. We therefore refer to such systems as “emitters”. The waves sent out by emitters can be analyzed to obtain information about the emitters themselves. This is done by receiving the waves and analyzing them.
In a scenario where we are moving, one of the (many) challenges faced when analyzing received signals is to find the precise geolocation of emitters and track them over time.
We therefore propose the hackathon challenge for EDTH Munich 2025, with the following sub-challenges, to be completed by teams of up to 5 hackers:
main challenge:
- geolocation of emitters
- tracking of emitters
Support challenge: Visualization of the analysis
We provide synthetic data in three sets, two for training and one for evaluation.
Note: The data is (highly) synthetic and solely for the hackathon.

Name: Towed Communication Antennas for UUV

Name: Self-Powered Propulsion Systems for UUV

The challenge here is to investigate practical implementations of these mechanisms to maximize endurance and efficiency.
